the_bug: my candidate-clustering helper bucketed decision minutes with `dec//2*2`, rounding every decision minute DOWN to the even 2-minute boundary so 2m and 3m signals would merge. A 3m bar starting 09:42 CLOSES AT 09:45. Rounding its decision minute to 09:44 presented its close one minute before that close existed.
why_it_is_a_leak_and_not_a_rounding_erro: the briefing stated the 3m candle's CLOSE as a completed fact at a minute when only two of its three minutes had elapsed. That is future information, full stop. The replay chart was correctly truncated - the leak was in the text I wrote beside it.
how_it_surfaced: the tv-trigger agent refused to adjudicate: 'the 3m signal candle starts 09:42 (3-min duration), so closes 09:45, but decision_minute/truncation is 09:44/09:43:59 - one minute before it can complete. Its close 30790.0 and same_candle claim are not knowable at the decision minute. Not guessing which is meant.' It returned constraints_failed ['briefing_incoherent'] rather than trading on it.
blast_radius: exactly two briefings, both on this day. (1) v5_d21_0902_trigger.json - the 3m 09:00 bar closes at 09:03, quoted at 09:02. (2) v5_d21_0944_trigger.json - the 3m 09:42 bar closes at 09:45, quoted at 09:44. Every other adjudication this session used an even 3m decision minute where the rounding was a no-op: London 03:42 (3m 03:39 -> 03:42) and NY_PRE 09:06 (3m 09:03 -> 09:06) are both exact.
fix: the clustering rule is now: a cluster's decision minute is the MAXIMUM of its members' own decision minutes, never a rounded-down boundary, with an assertion that fails loudly if a cluster minute ever precedes a member's. Waiting a minute costs a minute of price; showing an unclosed bar costs the whole run.

his_ruling: 'if a genuinely valid short setup happens i wouldnt take it since im in longs, id either get out or move my trade to BE. depends on how the setup im currently in looks compared to setup that just fired. for example if the short is high conviction full trade and the long im in is light, i'll probably close and flip shorts, but that is HEAVY discretion from my end.'
what_this_changes: a valid opposing signal while in a position is a POSITION-MANAGEMENT event, not an entry event. My implementation had it as neither: position_already_open was an absolute bar, the candidate was passed, and NOTHING happened to the open trade. That is the one branch he would never take - ignoring it entirely.
the_ladder_he_described: hold - the held setup still looks better than the one that just fired
move_to_breakeven - the default when the new signal is real but not clearly stronger
close_and_flip - only when the new setup is clearly stronger than the held one; his example is a FULL-conviction short against a LIGHT long
HEAVY_DISCRETION: his words, and it means the rule cannot be mechanised into a single answer. What CAN be mechanised is that the decision gets made and recorded instead of skipped.
implementation: when a qualifying opposing signal fires while a position is open, the trigger now also emits a management action from that ladder with a rationale comparing the two setups - conviction, size class, and how each one's structure looks. The orchestrator applies it and logs it. The escalation gate still refuses the ESCALATION (Tier 1 cannot un-open a position, T25 safeguard 4 stands) but the candidate no longer just evaporates.
WHY_I_AM_SCORING_IT_BOTH_WAYS: this rule can cost real R and I do not want to bury that in an aggregate. Day 1 already contains one instance and it is expensive - see the note below. Every day from here reports day_r with the rule applied AND without, so he can rule on evidence.
